subject.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups

question: Should subscription-auth embedded dispatch remain a claude-cli rule in core with a new plugin runtime eligibility API, or should the Anthropic CLI backend declare a provider-owned capability consumed by generic core code?
rationale: Both shapes can fix the reproduced bug, but the choice establishes a durable plugin API and determines ownership of provider-specific billing and credential policy; repository policy favors provider ownership, while changing the branch requires explicit runtime-owner intent.

options.title: Use a provider capability
options.body: Move the claude-cli subscription-auth predicate into Anthropic-owned CLI backend metadata and have generic embedded-runner and timeout code consume one dispatch plan.

options.title: Approve the core rule
options.body: Keep the current core allowlist and plugin runtime helper, but explicitly accept the new public contract and require compatibility coverage for future auth modes and providers.

options.title: Pause broader dispatch work
options.body: Limit or close this branch until a narrower active-memory workaround or a broader embedded CLI execution design is agreed.

recommendation.title: Use a provider capability
recommendation.body: Move the claude-cli subscription-auth predicate into Anthropic-owned CLI backend metadata and have generic embedded-runner and timeout code consume one dispatch plan.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most directly connects this person to both plugin-runtime contracts and agent/provider execution policy.
